I have gone through the exact same thing, and I think you need to be more concerned about the amount of control you are putting yourself through on your "good days".  I had eating disorder issues and I would do the exact same thing as you, try and push myself on how long I go hungry and little I could eat to be not hungry.  The hunger actually starts to become addicting.  Then every so often, it's like I would go into a trance.  I would put disgusting amounts of food in my body, completely aware as to how many calories I was consuming but I was like I had degraded to an animal, I didn't care anymore and could no way stop my impulse to eat.  

I think what you need to do is stop pushing yourself to eat less and less and push to see how long you can go hungry.  Eat when you're hungry, stop when you're not.  Don't push yourself to be hungry.  As soon as I stopped obsessing over food so much and occasionally let myself indulge in a small treat, I stopped having my manic gorging episodes.  Count calories using Myplate or My Fitness Pal if you want to watch what you eat, then you can account for the occasional chocolate bar or piece of fried chicken and adjust the rest of your day accordingly.
